eventExplanations.1: Measured from the last entry into this block using game ticks, not elapsed wall-clock seconds. The original compares unsigned 32-bit elapsed time and threshold.
eventExplanations.2: Reads the specified player gold balance. The comparison is strict: equality does not match.
eventExplanations.3: Reads the specified player gold balance. The comparison is strict: equality does not match.
eventExplanations.4: Reads this exact object-class counter, not a combined family of units, animals or construction sites. Equality does not match; the count and threshold use unsigned comparison.
eventExplanations.5: Reads this exact object-class counter, not a combined family of units, animals or construction sites. Equality does not match; the count and threshold use unsigned comparison.
eventExplanations.6: Checks slot allocation, not health. An object queued for deletion still fails this condition until removed; a never-used slot already satisfies it.
eventExplanations.7: Reads the slot coordinates without checking whether it is live. A removed slot can retain its former position. Coordinates are compared exactly, without byte wrapping.
eventExplanations.8: Tests exactly zero, not a low-happiness threshold. Does not check slot allocation; retained or unused slot fields can also match.
eventExplanations.9: Does not check whether the slot is live. Compares the requested owner integer exactly, unlike the byte-normalized ownership-setting command.
eventExplanations.10: Uses stored tile coordinates without a live-slot check. Distance exactly3 does not match; a nonzero slot compared with itself does. First slot0 always fails.
eventExplanations.11: Compares zero/nonzero states, not exact integer values. Any nonzero expected value matches any nonzero stored value.
eventExplanations.12: Runs only when game tick %36 is0. Uses the local player, not the script player. Matches exact object class or held-item class; radius3 includes its boundary.
eventExplanations.13: Runs only when game tick %36 is1. Matches the exact unit-type byte with no owner or unit-class restriction; radius3 includes its boundary. Zero is an exact no-sex test, not an any-type sentinel.
eventExplanations.14: Runs only when game tick %36 is2 and it is night. Searches the center tile for corpse class58 with the burning flag, not a radius around it.

propertyExplanations.-1:2: The original accepts only jobs listed for the unit type; any other request clears the job to zero.
propertyExplanations.-1:3: Uses the health helper: negative requests become zero and health is capped by the current maximum. This is a stat change, not an attack; setting zero does not itself call the damage/deletion routine.
propertyExplanations.-1:4: Uses the original 16-bit maximum-health field. Reducing the maximum also caps current health; raising it does not fill or proportionally scale current health.
propertyExplanations.-1:5: Clamped to0..100. This does not start reproduction or pregnancy. Normal mating still checks both partners, their actions/activities, a suitable home and AI conditions.
propertyExplanations.-1:7: Calls SetTarget only if the referenced slot is live at execution time. Slot zero is not a special clear-target request.
propertyExplanations.-1:8: The stored byte is one-based: 1 means player0; zero normally selects other owners. Cows bypass this owner test. These filters apply to monster prey searches, not every attack-selection routine.
propertyExplanations.-1:9: Nonzero compares the exact object class. Zero selects the default villager/cow candidates; it does not mean all object classes. Used by monster prey searches.
propertyExplanations.-1:10: Zero disables this unit-type test; nonzero requires the exact sex/unit-type byte. Other class, owner and visibility checks still apply.
propertyExplanations.-1:12: Writes a class-specific byte. Only generator171/226 use it as the generated object class.
propertyExplanations.-1:14: Controls flag 0x200000: resident food/water/church/mating choices and idle wandering are affected. This is separate from the automatic-work flag.
propertyExplanations.-1:16: State is a byte whose interpretation depends on the object class; it is not the activity number.
propertyExplanations.-1:17: Transfers ownership, updates the main object player counts and destination occupancy, and changes its color. The directly linked object also receives the owner/color. Existing action, job and targets are not cleared by this helper.
propertyExplanations.-1:18: Writes the path-coordinate byte directly; this is not a move order and does not compute a new path.
propertyExplanations.-1:19: Writes the path-coordinate byte directly; this is not a move order and does not compute a new path.
propertyExplanations.-1:20: Controls invulnerability flag 0x800000. Demon attacks bypass this flag; on fire objects it also prevents normal health decay.
propertyExplanations.-1:21: Activity meanings depend on the object class; no confirmed label is available for this target.
propertyExplanations.-1:23: Stores the attack-target reference and enables the forced-attack flag. It does not immediately issue a movement order.
propertyExplanations.-1:24: Controls flag 0x10000000. For unselected villagers/creatures the AI can flee from a target or search for a threat. Selection, attack state and other checks still gate fleeing; clearing this flag does not prevent low-health or unarmed retreat.
propertyExplanations.-1:25: Stores a byte and recomputes the fixed-point speed factor: speed/48, then multiplied by1.5. The current tile can add the road multiplier. The value is not a percentage or a direct multiplier.
